race_name: L'Etape Chile by Tour de France

top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic L'Etape Chile by Tour de France's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before November.

Road-specific control matters at L'Etape Chile by Tour de France. Practice on coastal rollers through lush Valdivian rainforest: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 68 miles.
87ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
5,919ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
68 miles on coastal rollers through lush Valdivian rainforest burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
At L'Etape Chile by Tour de France, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of L'Etape Chile by Tour de France. Train it until it feels boring.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at L'Etape Chile by Tour de France. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on coastal rollers through lush Valdivian rainforest can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 5,919ft of climbing on coastal rollers through lush Valdivian rainforest does to your power file on race day.
5,919ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for L'Etape Chile by Tour de France’s 68 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at L'Etape Chile by Tour de France requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on coastal rollers through lush valdivian rainforest to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, Road Specific, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 68 miles of coastal rollers through lush valdivian rainforest in Valdivia, Los Rios, Chile.
